title: Muscle strains
intro: A muscle strain is a stretch or small tear in a muscle or the tendon attached to it, usually from sudden overload during sport or lifting. It causes pain, tenderness and sometimes bruising. Most strains heal well within days to weeks with relative rest, gradual return to movement and sensible rehabilitation.

sections.heading: Causes and typical sites
paragraphs: Strains happen when a muscle is stretched beyond its capacity or contracts forcefully, such as when sprinting, kicking or lifting a heavy object. The thigh muscles, calf, groin and lower back are commonly affected. Risk rises with fatigue, inadequate warm-up, earlier injury and sudden increases in training.

sections.heading: Symptoms and severity
paragraphs: Mild strains cause tightness and soreness. Moderate strains cause sharp pain, swelling, bruising and weakness. A severe tear may cause a pop, a visible gap or inability to use the muscle. Pain worsens when the muscle is stretched or contracted.

sections.heading: First steps
paragraphs: In the first days, reduce activity that provokes pain but avoid complete immobilisation. Cool packs for short periods can ease pain, and compression and elevation reduce swelling. Simple painkillers may help. Early gentle movement within comfortable limits promotes healing better than prolonged rest.

sections.heading: Rehabilitation and return to sport
paragraphs: As pain settles, start gentle stretching and strengthening, increasing gradually. Return to sport only when you can move without pain, have regained strength and flexibility, and can perform sport-specific actions. Returning too early often leads to re-injury. A physiotherapist can guide a safe plan, especially after repeated strains.

sections.heading: When to see a doctor
paragraphs: Seek medical advice if you cannot walk or use the muscle, heard a pop with severe weakness, have a visible deformity, intense swelling or numbness, or if pain does not improve after a week or so. Warm up, build training gradually and stop when you feel sharp pain to reduce the risk of strains.

examples.title: Returning to running
examples.text: Imagine you pulled your calf during a run. You could walk and stretch gently, add light strengthening after a few days, and return to running with short sessions only when you feel no pain.

examples.title: Seeking advice
examples.text: Suppose a thigh injury leaves a visible dent and you cannot straighten your leg. You might go to an emergency department or sports medicine clinic for assessment.
